The legal precedents mentioned in the text are Smith v. Maryland and Jones v. United States. Smith v. Maryland established the third-party doctrine, which posits that individuals do not have a reasonable expectation of privacy for information voluntarily shared with third parties. Jones v. United States applied this principle, referencing Smith to uphold the same idea. Without specific details about the "case at hand" in your query, I can note that these precedents are relevant to any case involving whether a person retains privacy rights over information disclosed to third parties, such as phone records or digital data.

The largest country in the world is Russia.
